## Challenge Description

![[HNF26 13.png]]

The challenge provided an encoded text block along with a short hint:

> [!todo] Description
>
> i do a rotate and some 2^6

Ciphertext:

```

```

The title "13" and the phrase "i do a rotate and some 2^6" pointed directly to the operations needed:

- "rotate" paired with the title suggested ROT13.
- $2^6 = 64$, pointing to Base64 encoding.
- Extending the theme of 13, the payload looked like it had been wrapped in Base64 13 times.

I tested this in CyberChef. An initial `ROT13` operation followed by 13 chained `From Base64` operations decoded the string completely.

![[HNF26 13 2.png]]

> [!note] Repeated Base64 layers
> Encoding text repeatedly with Base64 makes it about a third larger each time, so the blob shrinks by the same factor as each layer is removed. That is why the final result is only a few bytes long. After ROT13, the text starts with `Vm0w`, which is the well-known look of text that has been Base64-encoded many times over, so it was a quick sign that more layers were hiding underneath.

The same process can be automated with a short Python script. It reads the ciphertext from `cipher.txt`:

```python
import base64
import codecs
from pathlib import Path

data = Path("cipher.txt").read_text().strip()

# Apply ROT13 once
data = codecs.decode(data, "rot_13")

# Decode Base64 13 times
for _ in range(13):
    data = base64.b64decode(data).decode("utf-8")

print(data)
```

Running it printed the flag:

```bash
┌──(nepz㉿nepz)-[~]
└─$ python3 solve.py
HNF26{base64_to_the_max}
```

> [!NOTE] Flag
> HNF26{base64_to_the_max}
